newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks zigzag to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks zigzag to higher close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks zigzagged to close higher on Tuesday, shedding some of the morning's gains due to uncertainty over the outlook for property prices in a major government land auction, brokers said.
"This is the largest site released by government in some time and one where a developer can actually add some value," said Steven Brown, research director at NAVA SC Securities.

The Hang Seng Index closed 83.39 points, or 0.65 percent, higher at 12,832.53, well off the day's high of 12,914.89. Turnover was a heavy HK$10.33 billion, substantially higher than Monday's HK$8.17 billion.

The market leaped a 150 points at the open on the back of the Dow's 100-point gain to 6,905.25 overnight. The New York index gained on the view the market had already taken into account a small interest rate hike.
The U.S. Federal Reserve policy-setting committee meets later on Tuesday to review lending rates, and most brokers are betting on a small, if any rate rise.
"I don't think there will be a rate hike," said David Williamson, director at W.I.Carr.
The local market also seems to have discounted any small interest rate hike.
The market zigzagged in the afternoon on concerns that prices paid at the land auction would be less than expected.
At the market's close at 0800 GMT, bids for the large Chai Wan site had topped HK$11 billion, already a positive sign.
The 25,592 sq metre site sold for HK$11.82 billion after more than two hours of bidding, with industry sources saying Sino Land was the buyer.
Sino closed down HK$0.05 at HK$8.45.
Bidders were also said to include Chueng Kong, whose share price fell HK$0.75 to HK$70.00, CITIC Pacific which put on HK$0.20 to HK$38.80, and China Overseas which eased HK$0.025 to HK$4.375.
New World Development added HK$0.30 to HK$43.20. The company reported first-half earnings of HK$2.2 billion, a 29.16 percent increase over the year-earlier period.

The Hang Seng China Enterprise Index lost 1.54 percent compared with the blue chip index's 0.65 percent gain, despite news that nine H-share companies would be allowed to continue to pay income tax at a preferential rate of 15 percent.
Of those maintaining the preferential tax rate, index heavyweights Shanghai Petrochemical slipped HK$0.055 to HK$1.97 and Yizheng Chemical 1033. HK gained HK$0.01 to HK$1.63.
